# SQL Server Analysis Services

Microsoft's OLAP layer. A **multidimensional** SSAS project sits on top of a relational mart and
declares, as XML source files: a data source (`.ds`), a data source view binding specific tables
(`.dsv`), one `.dim` per dimension, one `.cube` per cube with its measure groups, and a
`.partitions` file. [[data-warehousing-and-business-intelligence]] holds **three** such projects.

| Project | Cube(s) | Over |
|---|---|---|
| `olap/ssas/` | `Adventure Works2019.cube` | the five `mart` tables — four `.dim` files |
| `project/twtr/ssas/` | `Twitter.cube` | `FactTwitterData` + `DimDate` |
| `project/twtr/ssas/` | `Twitter_rsi.cube` | `FactRSI` + `DimRSI` + `DimDate` |

The AdventureWorks cube's measure group exposes quantity, unit price, discount, line total and a
row count, with the time dimension **role-played twice** as order date and ship date — the OLAP
expression of the same modelling choice made in the DDL. See [[star-schema]] and
[[measure-vs-dimension]].

## The SSAS side ships the design the SQL side rejects

This is the sharpest finding in the repository. `docs/star-schema.md` argues at length that a
technical indicator belongs on the fact table as a measure, with thresholds pushed into a view —
[[rsi-as-measure-not-dimension]]. And `project/twtr/ssas/Dim RSI.dim` implements the indicator **as a
dimension**, with `RSIKey`, `IsOverbought` and `IsOversold` attributes, feeding a second cube whose
only measure is a row count.

Both artefacts are committed. The winner ships in SQL; the loser ships in SSAS. See
[[keep-the-superseded-version-in-tree]].

## Three further drifts

- `Twitter.dsv` binds `FactTwitterData` and `DimDate`; `Twitter_rsi.dsv` binds `FactRSI` and
  `DimRSI`. **None of those four tables is created by any committed DDL**, which builds
  `dw.FACT_QUOTES`, `dw.DIM_DATE` and `dw.DIM_TICKER`. The cubes and the schema do not describe the
  same database.
- `olap/ssas/DIM TIME.dim` exposes only `DateKey`, `Day`, `Month` and `Year`, while the DDL defines
  Quarter, MonthName and IsWeekend as well. The cube sees a narrower dimension than the mart offers.
- All of it is [[documentation-drift]] of the kind that only surfaces when someone tries to process
  the cube.

## Never deployed

> "They are Visual Studio project files rather than deployed databases; opening them needs SQL Server
> Data Tools."
> — Data-Warehousing-and-Business-Intelligence/docs/star-schema.md, 2026-07-25

Stated by the repo itself, which is the honest move — [[provenance-and-limits-stated-inline]]. The
`.dim`, `.cube` and `.partitions` files are committed as plain blobs with no `.gitattributes` and no
Git LFS.
